tasks.title: Capital.com WebSocket client: OHLC bid/ask subscription, 10-minute ping, auto-reconnect
acceptance_criteria: reconnect survives forced disconnect test
ping loop verified
subscribe and ping replies are validated; stale tokens, missing or error replies cause reconnect with a fresh session
owner-run verify_capital_stream.py shows both bid and ask updates arriving on the demo stream
tasks.completion_note: Implemented authenticated Capital.com minute OHLC subscriptions for configured epics, bid/ask update normalization, eight-minute WebSocket keepalive, bounded reconnect, and REST backfill beginning at the last observed minute to recover incomplete candles. Forced-disconnect, resubscription, gap-fill, ping, and epic-limit tests pass in GitHub Actions run 37119657855. Ready for Claude review in PR #5. CLAUDE REVIEW 1 (changes requested). Approved as written: epic cap 40, token-bearing messages never logged by this module, 8-minute ping, bounded reconnect backoff, REST backfill from the last observed minute, strict numeric validation, bid and ask both captured, offline tests with forced disconnect. Required changes: (1) Silent-failure risk. Subscribe and ping replies are ignored, so a subscription made with stale session tokens (REST session idle more than 10 minutes) fails without any signal and the socket just sits open. Do all three: (a) call the REST client's ping() before every connection attempt so the tokens are fresh; (b) read the subscribe reply and treat any non-OK status, or any requested epic not confirmed, as a failure that closes the socket and reconnects with a fresh session (log epic names and status only); (c) require a reply to each ping within 30 seconds and treat a missing or non-OK reply as a dead connection. Liveness must rest on ping replies, not on price flow, because markets are legitimately silent when closed. Add tests for stale-token subscribe error, missing ping reply and non-OK ping reply. (2) websockets DEBUG logging prints frames, including the cst and securityToken fields. Force logging.getLogger('websockets') to WARNING at import of this module (and in configure_logging) and add a test that DEBUG records from it cannot be emitted. (3) Exceptions raised inside the on_update callback are currently caught by the generic reconnect handler and look like network errors. Let consumer exceptions propagate out of run_forever (log type only) so a bug in the recorder is visible and supervised, not hidden in a reconnect loop. Add a test. (4) Add scripts/verify_capital_stream.py for the owner to run on the pod: demo-only guard as in verify_capital_demo.py, argument --epic (default US100) and --seconds (default 90), prints redacted JSON only: counts of bid and ask updates, first and last update time, whether ping reply was OK, number of reconnects, and the epic. No tokens, no account data. Document in infra/runpod/README.md that on weekends the owner can pass --epic BTCUSD as a test-only stream (BTCUSD is never added to instruments.yaml and never traded). Live verification on the pod is the acceptance for this task. CODEX REVIEW-CYCLE 1 FIXES: validates REST session before each connection; checks subscribe acknowledgements for OK status and each configured epic; validates immediate and periodic ping acknowledgements with a 30-second timeout; logs websockets at WARNING; logs callback exception type and propagates the original exception; adds the demo-only owner verification script and RunPod instructions. Also addresses automated PR review: naive snapshotTimeUTC is interpreted as UTC and REST gap-fill starts at the earliest side watermark while suppressing per-side duplicates. Full CI run 37120689237 passed (lint, typecheck, migrations, tests, handoff validation, secret scan, Docker/runtime and backup/restore). Code is ready for Claude re-review; live pod verification remains pending under Q-019.

files: scripts/validate_tick_data.py (HistData tick files carry bid and ask)

review_notes: Tooling review only (answer to Q-038: option 1). The empirical report stays blocked on B-007 (recorder overlap). After these fixes set T-017 back to 'blocked' with the evidence; the numbers are produced on the Pod by the runner below.

1. Iterables are consumed more than once. calibrate() loops over capital_bars three times (basis map, capital_spreads, session spreads). A generator, which is what a Parquet reader gives, is empty after the first pass, so a real run would silently report zero Capital.com spreads. Materialize each input once (or compute all statistics in a single pass) and add a test that passes generators.
2. Recorder rows are written for both sides and both carry spread_close, so capital spreads are counted twice. Use the bid rows only (or dedupe by timestamp). Test it.

3. Spec asks for spread statistics (median, p90, p99) per instrument and per session for HistData ticks as well as Capital.com. HistData ticks are never assigned to a session and the written report shows only one summary row with p90 only. Add per-session tables (n, median, p90, p99) for basis, HistData spread and Capital.com spread, per instrument, in docs/reports/basis_and_spread.md.

4. Sessions are hard-coded UTC hour ranges in _default_session. Read session windows from the same configuration MarketHours uses (src/trader/data/market_hours.py); keep a hard-coded fallback only for tests. If the config has no named sessions, ask in a question rather than inventing them.

5. The timezone check is not proven: the only test uses one 10-minute window at lag 0. Add a test where HistData is the same series shifted by one hour and the tool reports best lag 1 (and timezone_ok false for expected 0), and one with shifted by zero that reports 0.

6. Spec: 'export to config-style parameters used by the PaperBroker and the backtester ... saved with lineage'. Add write_cost_model(results, path, lineage) that writes per-instrument per-session median/p90/p99 spreads and basis, with lineage (input file names and sha256, row counts, date ranges, generated_at, git commit if available). It must refuse to write (and say why) when a session has fewer samples than a stated minimum (put the minimums in the function signature with defaults, for example 1000 spread samples and 500 basis minutes) so provisional defaults remain until real data exists. Do not change any PaperBroker cost.

7. Add a runner so the Pod step is one command: python -m trader.data.calibration --histdata <dir> --recorder <dir> --instrument NAS100 --report <md path> --cost-model <yaml path>. It reads Parquet with pyarrow in chunks and prints the output paths. Outputs go to the path given (the Pod will use /workspace). Test the argument parsing and a tiny Parquet fixture end to end.

8. Memory: spread lists hold every tick in Python lists, which will not fit a year of NAS100 ticks. Use bounded memory (numpy arrays per chunk, or a fixed-width histogram for percentiles) and test with a generator of many rows.
Non-blocking: replace the 'for _ in [0]' walrus trick in hist_spreads with a plain loop.

1. Trailing exits are silently ignored: _exit_rules reads the trailing rule and _OpenTrade stores trailing_distance/trailing_activation, but run_backtest never uses them, so a spec with a trailing exit backtests as if it had none. Implement it (activate after activation_distance of favourable move, then stop ratchets distance behind the best price; ratchet only on bars already closed so the same bar cannot both move and trigger it) or raise ValueError for unsupported trailing rules. 2. Optimistic fills: a stop is filled at stop_level even when the bar opens beyond it (gap), and the entry bar is never checked for stop/target although the position opens at that bar's open. 3. Re-entry ordering: after an exit on a bar the same bar's open is used for a new entry that happened earlier in time than the exit. Do not enter on the bar an exit occurred; wait for the next bar.

4. max_drawdown and equity_curve are realized-only. Mark the open position to the bar close (unrealized P&L) in the curve and drawdown, or name the fields realized_* and document it; the validator will gate on drawdown so it must not be understated.

Blocking: (1) CI will fail: ruff reports 124 errors in the T-070 files (43 E702 and 28 E701 multiple statements per line, 40 E501 line too long, imports) and 6 files are not ruff-formatted. Run ruff check --fix, ruff format, then fix the rest by hand; mypy src/trader must stay clean. Do not paste dense one-line code. (2) Singleton protection is not fail-safe: Worker.is_scalable() allows anything with role=='worker' and no core/singleton tag, and RunPodClient._pod defaults a missing role to 'worker', so an untagged core pod would be scaled down. Make it default-deny: only pods carrying the tag managed_by=ai-trader-autoscaler are ever terminated, in evaluate() and reconcile_orphans(); add tests where an untagged pod, a core pod and a singleton-tagged pod are never targeted in the idle, spend-cap and orphan paths. (3) Acceptance 'load test scales up and down' is not met: test_scaling.py only covers create and the spend cap. Add a simulated load test: rising depth and age creates workers up to max_workers, then idle for idle_minutes terminates down to min_workers, never below. (4) RunPodClient does not satisfy the RunPodWorkerApi protocol the autoscaler uses: list_workers returns PodInfo (no is_scalable or cpu_percent) and create_worker needs image and env but the protocol passes only tags. Add an adapter or align the types, and test the autoscaler against the real client with an httpx MockTransport. The endpoint https://api.runpod.io/v2/pods looks like the serverless API; check the current RunPod REST docs for pod create, list and terminate and cite the doc in the evidence. No live calls. (5) WorkerRunner timeout is not enforced: 'with ThreadPoolExecutor' waits for the handler on exit, so a hung handler blocks the worker. Use pool.shutdown(wait=False, cancel_futures=True) or a subprocess boundary, and test with a handler that sleeps past the timeout. (6) Priority ordering is only sorted inside one claimed batch; with count=1 P3 can run before P0. Use one stream per priority and claim P0 first, or document and test the limit. review_notes: Cycle 2 of 2. V-140 items 1, 2, 3 (re-validate at confirm), 4, 5, 9 and 10 are fixed and verified. Four items remain; fix exactly these, anything new from me after this goes to the owner as a question.

B1 (blocker). Gate settings never reach the real config. strategy_lab.yaml is nested (gate1_backtest_to_paper.min_trades) but _persist writes flat keys such as gate1_min_trades at the top level, so the value is ignored or the strict loader (trader.core.config.load_config_file) rejects the file on restart. Add an explicit key to (file, path) map, using the same names as _check_strategy_floors in core/config.py (gate1_min_trades -> gate1_backtest_to_paper.min_trades and so on; risk keys stay top level in risk.yaml). Also, when the file does not yet exist in /workspace/config, seed the document from the checked-in default in config/ before changing the key (today a missing file is written with a single key, which fails the loader). Test: copy the real config/risk.yaml and config/strategy_lab.yaml into tmp_path, apply one risk change and one gate change through the service, then load them with load_all_configs and assert the new values and that nothing else changed.

B2 (blocker). A scheduled loosening can overwrite a later tightening. Example: loosening 0.5 to 0.75 is scheduled for tomorrow, the owner then tightens to 0.25 today, and apply_due writes 0.75 over it. In apply_due re-validate against the CURRENT value: the stored old_value must equal the current value, and bounds and consistency must still pass; otherwise drop it with an audit entry and a notification. Also refuse a new request for a key that already has a scheduled change, and prune expired pending changes inside request_change (today an expired pending blocks that key with 'already pending' until someone confirms it). Tests for both.

B3 (blocker). Apply is not fully transactional: _persist runs first, then version_store.append; if the store fails, the file is already changed while memory is not. Write the version-store record first or restore the previous file contents when the store fails, and test with a failing store that file and memory both keep the old value.

B4 (blocker, small). halt_active defaults to a callable that always returns False, so a wiring mistake silently disables the halt gate. Make halt_active a required argument (tests pass lambda: False explicitly). Also route revert() through request_change so its refusals are audited.

Non-blocking follow-ups (not required now): declare load_pending/save_pending on the SettingsVersionStore Protocol instead of getattr; add a resolve_startup path for the owner to clear the startup refusal; fsync before the rename; remove leftover temp files on failure.

tasks.title: Strategy Lab progress during loading and mining; reclaim dead-pid lock
acceptance_criteria: runner.py writes progress.json BEFORE and DURING data loading and candidate mining (phase names like loading:<instrument>:<tf>m and mining:<instrument>:<tf>m), not only after all groups are built; write_progress and its state are defined before the first load. Keep the lab_run.py placeholder only as a fallback.

A heartbeat (updated_at timestamp, ISO UTC) is written at least every 60 seconds while a long phase runs (a daemon thread or per-chunk call), so a silent stage cannot look like a hang; progress.json always includes pid, started_at and updated_at.

RunFileLock stores the pid; on acquire, if the lock exists and its pid is not alive (os.kill(pid, 0) fails), the lock is reclaimed with a logged note instead of refusing. A live pid still refuses. Unit tests cover live, dead and malformed lock files.

tasks.title: Strategy Lab memory: slim evaluation results, release memory between instruments, measure the parent spike
acceptance_criteria: Measurements (run 20261009T220740Z on image bc1f9354, 4 workers, V-283): loading is NOT the problem (main RSS 0.28-0.42 GB, anon 0.47-0.59 GB; mining 0.5 GB and under 0.1 s for seeds). The spike is in the evaluation stage: evaluating:0/20:NSXUSD:5m main RSS 8.7 GB + worker PSS 3.5 GB = cgroup anon 10.2 GB, finished in 251 s; after 20/20 the parent still held 5.4 GB RSS (5.6 GB anon); the next group evaluating:0/20:XAUUSD:5m reached main 6.6 GB + workers 9.3 GB = cgroup anon 15.06 GB and was stopped.

Find why the PARENT reaches 8.7 GB in pipeline.run (src/trader/lab/pipeline.py). Prime suspects: _CandidateEvaluation objects returned from workers carry full BacktestResult trade lists, equity curves, neighbour and regime results and are all held in the evaluations dict; in_sample_times set and tuple copies of the candle frames; Candle object tuples rebuilt from columnar data. Profile with tracemalloc or sizeof on a synthetic multi-year 5m frame and report the largest items in the handoff.

Fix 1: workers return only what the parent needs (gate1 metric dict, verdict, hash, small summaries); trade lists, equity curves and full BacktestResult stay in the worker and are dropped there. Decisions and ledger records must be identical for the same input (test: old-path and slim-path give equal metrics and verdicts).

Fix 2: release memory between instrument/timeframe groups. Preferred: run each group in its own forked child process that returns only the slim decisions, so the OS frees everything; acceptable alternative: del the group data, gc.collect(), and show by measurement that parent RSS returns near its pre-group level. After NSXUSD 20/20 the parent must not still hold 5 GB.

Fix 3: workers must not copy the parent: share the frame read-only (fork) and avoid touching objects that cause copy-on-write (build tuples before forking, avoid per-worker re-expansion of columnar data). Report worker PSS per worker.

Benchmark locally on a synthetic multi-year 5m frame (about 400k bars) with 20 seed specs: report parent peak RSS, worker PSS and wall time before and after; target parent peak under 3 GB and total anon under 8 GB for both instruments sequentially with 4 workers. Do not raise the worker cap without evidence.

Do NOT change the 12 GB real-memory stop; keep per-phase memory_diagnostics. tasks.title: ATR-scaled exits: stop and target distances as ATR multiples
acceptance_criteria: Evidence (T-121 run, rev 302): random-entry gross per trade is -0.97 points (NSXUSD) and -0.13 (XAUUSD) even before costs, and zero-cost seed runs show the same -0.9 and -0.1: every seed and pattern used stop 1.5 and target 1.0 as ABSOLUTE POINTS, but the average 5m range is about 16 points on NSXUSD and 2.2 on XAUUSD. With distances far inside one bar the engine resolves each trade by its pessimistic stop-first rule, so no strategy can win. The seeds (for example ema_crossover_atr_stop) were meant to be ATR multiples.

Seeds, pattern miner and the controls random-entry use unit atr with their existing numbers as multiples.
Unit tests: atr exits scale ten-fold with ten-fold volatility, random entries with atr exits have no large gross edge or loss, default unit is points.

tasks.title: Movement-matching study: how often did the same price movement repeat and what followed
acceptance_criteria: Why (D-038 and owner request 2026-10-13): the owner wants the agent to find out how many times a market movement repeated in past years and what followed, comparing the shape of movement, not exact values. Price only; no news or macro inputs. Diagnostic only: nothing counts as a Gate 1 pass or feeds the trial counter, ledger or promotion files, no gate or cost config is edited, the sealed 3-month holdout stays sealed, no paper trading, no broker calls. Claude writes the detailed design note docs/specs/t146_movement_matching.md before Codex starts; this task starts only after that note exists and T-145 is accepted.

Method (fixed in advance): cut each series into windows of N candles (N chosen from a small pre-registered set, for example 30, 60, 120); express each window as moves from its start divided by ATR at that time so quiet and wild periods are comparable; measure similarity with an elastic distance (dynamic time warping with a band limit) and also a plain correlation baseline; match only against data strictly before the window being matched (no look-ahead); remove overlapping matches (a match within one window length of a better match counts once); for each match record the forward move at fixed horizons (for example 6, 12, 30 candles) in ATR and points, the direction, and the time it took.

Statistics: report per shape-cluster how many distinct matches there were, the share that went up and down, the average forward move, and the same numbers for matched random windows (same count, same time spread) so we can see if the shape beats random. Count every shape and parameter tried (the number of trials) and report it next to every result. Net the forward move of costs (NSXUSD about 4 points, XAUUSD about 1.6 points per trade, from the T-143 evidence) before calling anything useful.

Scope: NSXUSD and XAUUSD on 1m, 3m, 5m (main) and 60m (extra), 1m mandatory; history 2022 through the day before the sealed holdout, with a clear in-sample period and a later out-of-sample period fixed in advance (state the split date). Report a result as found only if it holds in the out-of-sample period.

Execution safety as in T-145: report CPU and RAM first, plan disjoint parallel work before launching, 13 GB total cap, per-worker RSS watchdog, checkpoints, no-progress stop, exit-code wrapper. Evidence docs/evidence/t146_matching_summary.json plus a plain-language report with a few example charts (shape, its matches, what followed). CI-importable unit tests, ruff check and format clean. PR, ONE log entry, validation entry, set to review, hand the turn to claude.

Design note written: follow docs/specs/t146_movement_matching.md (split dates, parameters, shape cards and overview charts per owner request 2026-10-16 22:36). Where this list and the note differ, the note is the newer one.

Changes requested V-377: (1) bound the scan: correlation pre-filter keeps the best 200 candidates per query, DTW only on those, plus LB_Keogh early abandon; pre-register a deterministic query sample (every m-th out-of-sample window, at most 2000 queries per symbol/timeframe/length) and state it in the evidence; run 60m first and report the measured time per group before 1m; (2) implement section 5 clusters (k-medoids on DTW over a sample of at most 3000 in-sample windows, k in {8,16,32}) and per-cluster in-sample and out-of-sample results vs random control, net of cost; (3) overview chart per symbol/timeframe; (4) mark each result found only if out-of-sample, net of cost and significant after Bonferroni on the full trial count (include cluster k and method in the count); (5) plain-language report with a verdict per symbol/timeframe. Keep the existing tests and add tests for the bounded scan and cluster assignment. The real-lake run still needs the Pod (Q-058); do not wait for it to finish these code changes.

decisions.statement: The LLM never has broker access. Proposals go through the deterministic Risk Guardian, then the Execution Service.
Stop/pause/kill must work without the LLM (deterministic fast path).
3M candles are produced by resampling 1M because Capital.com has no 3-minute resolution.
HistData is used for hypothesis generation; Capital.com demo forward testing is used for confirmation. HistData is bid-only, M1, EST without DST; convert to UTC on import.
Start with one RunPod pod (ROLE=all, CPU only); split into core and worker, and move to managed Postgres/Redis, before live trading.

Telegram is the primary natural-language channel; the web UI is optional and sits behind the same ChatChannel interface. Decided by Claude on the owner's delegation: Telegram is the interface, with a web chat added later if wanted.
Strategies are declarative specs run in a sandbox; no LLM-written executable code runs in core or execution processes.
Backups: GitHub for code/config/state, HuggingFace for data and results. Never back up secrets.
Account size for risk sizing means account equity (balance plus open P&L).
Starting risk limits: 0.5% risk per trade, 2% max daily loss, 10% max drawdown, 3 concurrent live strategies.

Risk limits and Lab gates can be changed by the owner through natural language, but only via the deterministic SettingsService: allow-listed owner chat, confirmation, hard ceilings baked into the image, tightening immediate, loosening needs a second factor and a cooldown, no loosening while a loss halt is active. LLM agents cannot call or edit it.
GitHub namespace Tarek-Assaf; private repos. Proposed names: ai-trader (GitHub) and ai-trader-data (HuggingFace dataset). HuggingFace username confirmed as Tarek-Assaf.
Reports and alerts go through Telegram plus email (address and method pending, Q-006).

The earlier project is reference material. Fresh repo with the new architecture; audit the old project first (C-005) and adopt pieces selectively. Nothing is adopted without passing this project's tests and safety invariants, and any model or signal from it enters only through the Strategy Lab gates.
v1 timeframes: 1M, 3M and 5M. 3M is resampled from 1M; 15M can be added later through config.
Email reports use SMTP with an app password held as a RunPod Secret (REPORT_EMAIL_TO holds the recipient). Telegram stays the primary channel.
Hard ceilings in config/risk_ceilings.yaml: risk per trade 1.0%, daily loss 4%, drawdown 15%, concurrent live strategies 5.

Reuse of the earlier project follows docs/legacy_audit.md: adapt data QA, tick/spread handling, experiment logging, backtest structure and tests; skip its models, risk manager, paper engine, paper trades and requirements.txt. Models re-enter only through Strategy Lab gates.

Strategy Lab gates use the stricter minimums: Gate 1 at least 300 simulated trades (100 out-of-sample), 5 walk-forward windows, 3 validation periods; Gate 2 at least 4 weeks and 200 demo trades; Gate 3 at least 4 weeks and 100 micro-live trades. Other gate criteria unchanged.

Analyst roster v1 as in ARCHITECTURE.md section 5.2: AI analysts (Technical, News and Macro, Critic, Performance) plus code analysts (indicator/pattern engine, execution quality, data quality, Risk Guardian). Instrument knowledge lives in config playbooks.

Phase 0 uses uv 0.6.3 with committed uv.lock and exact direct dependency pins. In ROLE=all, root entrypoint only prepares /workspace ownership, then supervisord, PostgreSQL, Redis and API run as the non-root trader user; PostgreSQL and Redis bind to loopback.

Publish the container image to the private GitHub Container Registry package ghcr.io/tarek-assaf/ai-trader for RunPod. Pull authentication uses a GitHub classic PAT scoped to read:packages; rotate by adding a replacement token to RunPod, confirming image pull and /health, then revoking the old token.

Testing-phase LLM strategy (no live trading): mixed tiers. Cheap tier (small in-pod model or Haiku 4.5) for news sorting, summaries and tagging; mid tier (Haiku 4.5 or Sonnet 5.5) for researcher, analyst and critic; Sonnet 5.5 for the final decision; strongest tier (Opus 5.5 or Fable 5.1) unused until the system is profitable. Event-driven invocation, prompt caching, batch mode for Lab and reports, hard daily spend cap. Provider and exact models remain swappable by config and are to be compared in a bake-off before live trading. No GPU role in v1.
websockets (pinned 17.1) is added as a runtime dependency for the Capital.com streaming client (T-011); it was not on the original allowed list but is required and small.

Fast-lane process per docs/process_fastlane.md: Full vs Light review tiers, batching of related small tasks, Light tasks may start before a Full review finishes (never building on unreviewed Full code), recorder T-014 first after T-011 then T-012, T-013, T-015, T-016, T-017. Defects that would likely waste the single attempt: scripts/demo_round_trip.py reads the minimum stop distance from dealingRules.minStepDistance. Use those, never minStepDistance; if neither is present or its unit is not POINTS, abort before taking the one-shot marker. Update the test fixtures to the real field names. | The BUY stop is measured from the BID, not the ask, and the script derives it from the ask. Compute the stop from snapshot.bid: stop = floor_to_tick(bid - min_distance - margin) with margin = max(5 ticks, current spread, 10% of min_distance). The tightened stop (+1 tick) must still be at least min_distance below the bid; abort in preflight if not. | Add a --preflight option: does only reads (environment checks, flat check, market rules, computed size/stop/tightened stop) and prints the redacted plan JSON with no marker and no order, so the owner can run it first without spending the single attempt. The runbook should say: run --preflight first, then the real command. | Make the one-shot marker survive only a real attempt: preflight and validation failures before submission must not create it (already true) and the runbook must say a clean broker rejection of the open request with an account that is confirmed flat can be reported to the owner, who decides about a re-run.

validations.evidence: PR #39 head e2389d80; CI run 37275317330 failed. Required fixes: 1. CI is red on head e2389d80 (run 37275317330, quality job failed; the two PostgreSQL tests were expected to need CI). Fix and cite a green full run. I cannot read the job log from my environment, so include the failing test names in your response. 2. A normal server-side stop-out or take-profit must not pause trading. reconcile() currently marks a submitted record closed and sets mismatch=True, so every ordinary exit latches a durable pause and needs a manual resume. Treat a submitted record whose deal is gone as closed without mismatch (optionally confirm with get_activity). Also accept a broker position size smaller than the reserved size (partial closes are a supported feature) while still flagging a larger size. Tests: stop-out then submit next cycle works; partial close does not pause; larger size or unknown position still pauses. 3. The Guardian lease is only checked inside submit(), and the lease TTL is 30 s, so after about 30 s idle the next entry finds an expired Guardian lease and pauses the system. tick()/reconcile() must renew both leases every interval. A lost lease still pauses and alerts; no silent re-acquire mid-run. Test with a fake clock or a lease double that expires after idle. 4. There is no deterministic way out of a reserved or ambiguous record, so the first ambiguous order or crash after reservation deadlocks resume() forever (reconcile keeps returning mismatch). Add an operator-only resolve_intent(cycle_id, outcome, deal_id=None, reason) that works only while paused, never resends, is journaled with an alert, and is not reachable from any LLM-side module. Outcomes: matched (link to a broker position whose epic/direction/size/stop match the intent) or rejected (only when broker positions and get_activity show nothing for that dealReference). Use the get_activity result rather than discarding it. Tests: timeout-after-accept then resolve matched then resume works with no resubmission; process killed after reserve then resolve rejected then resume works and the cycle_id is still never reusable. 5. Acceptance criterion 'test that the LLM-side modules cannot reach it' is not covered: the AST test only proves place_order has one caller. Add an import-boundary test that nothing under agents/, lab/ or other LLM-side packages imports trader.execution.manager, journal, leader, reconciliation or brokers, directly or transitively.

validations.subject: T-028 review cycle 3 (Claude): held-open demo round trip and account mapping
validations.method: Read held_open preflight, round_trip and attempts evidence; compared account fields across the 13-poll series against the hypothesis.
validations.evidence: docs/evidence/t028_q040_held_open_round_trip_20261006.json; docs/evidence/t028_q040_held_open_attempts_20261006.json; docs/evidence/t028_q040_held_open_preflight_20261006.json
validations.review_notes: Cycle 3 evidence is sufficient. Held-open series: 13 polls over 62.6 s, position visible in 13/13 polls, distinct timestamps, flat confirmed, no URL/token. Observed open (0.001 US100, notional ~31.3 USD): first available 999.48, balance 999.79, deposit 999.79, profitLoss 0.0; last available 999.49, balance 999.80, deposit 999.79, profitLoss 0.01. Findings: (a) the IG-style hypothesis is WRONG: balance moved +0.01 together with profitLoss +0.01, so balance already includes unrealised P&L (balance = equity); equity = balance + profitLoss would double count. (b) margin used = balance - available (about 0.31, which is 1% of the notional), NOT deposit; deposit stayed 999.79 and looks like cash/realised funds. (c) cash = balance - profitLoss. (d) /accounts lags: after_close still showed available 999.49. (e) A second anomalous reading appeared (attempt 1 account_before: available 0, balance 0, deposit 999.8, profitLoss -999.8; same shape as the 13:24Z preflight): treat balance 0 with profitLoss = -deposit as an invalid snapshot. Caveats: precision is one cent at 0.001 size (D-027 said about 1.0, the smaller size is safer); the Pod image tag cannot be introspected in the container (expected tag efab3d8 recorded, accepted as a documented limitation). Attempt 1 position disappeared after about 30 s (the 6.3 point stop was probably hit) and the close returned 404 error.not-found.dealId; treat 404 on close as 'verify with /positions', not a failure. T-028 evidence criteria are met; the corrected mapping is NOT yet in code/config, so config verified stays false until T-086.

validations.method: Read the diff at b0d8a60, ran ruff check, ruff format --check and mypy locally on the changed files, compared the tests with the two acceptance criteria.

validations.review_notes: Cycle 1. Blocking: (1) CI will fail: ruff reports 124 errors in the T-070 files (43 E702 and 28 E701 multiple statements per line, 40 E501 line too long, imports) and 6 files are not ruff-formatted. Run ruff check --fix, ruff format, then fix the rest by hand; mypy src/trader must stay clean. Do not paste dense one-line code. (2) Singleton protection is not fail-safe: Worker.is_scalable() allows anything with role=='worker' and no core/singleton tag, and RunPodClient._pod defaults a missing role to 'worker', so an untagged core pod would be scaled down. Make it default-deny: only pods carrying the tag managed_by=ai-trader-autoscaler are ever terminated, in evaluate() and reconcile_orphans(); add tests where an untagged pod, a core pod and a singleton-tagged pod are never targeted in the idle, spend-cap and orphan paths. (3) Acceptance 'load test scales up and down' is not met: test_scaling.py only covers create and the spend cap. Add a simulated load test: rising depth and age creates workers up to max_workers, then idle for idle_minutes terminates down to min_workers, never below. (4) RunPodClient does not satisfy the RunPodWorkerApi protocol the autoscaler uses: list_workers returns PodInfo (no is_scalable or cpu_percent) and create_worker needs image and env but the protocol passes only tags. Add an adapter or align the types, and test the autoscaler against the real client with an httpx MockTransport. The endpoint https://api.runpod.io/v2/pods looks like the serverless API; check the current RunPod REST docs for pod create, list and terminate and cite the doc in the evidence. No live calls. (5) WorkerRunner timeout is not enforced: 'with ThreadPoolExecutor' waits for the handler on exit, so a hung handler blocks the worker. Use pool.shutdown(wait=False, cancel_futures=True) or a subprocess boundary, and test with a handler that sleeps past the timeout. (6) Priority ordering is only sorted inside one claimed batch; with count=1 P3 can run before P0. Use one stream per priority and claim P0 first, or document and test the limit. Non-blocking: flaky tests/unit/test_capital_rate_limit.py::test_two_clients_reuse_one_session_with_shared_http_client failed once on CI and passed on rerun (shared session cache across tests); isolate the cache in a fixture. questions.text: Please review T-009 / PR #1. Owner's RunPod Network Volume repeatedly triggers PostgreSQL invalid-permissions during initdb even though stat reports mode 700 after chmod. The PR adds a POSTGRES_DATA_DIR override for a smoke-only local path and documents that it is non-durable. Is this suitable to proceed with Phase 0 /health verification? Please also advise the durable PostgreSQL storage route for paper operation, given D-005 requires managed Postgres/Redis before live trading.
questions.answer: T-009 approved for smoke check only. Durable route for PAPER operation: keep PostgreSQL on the pod's container disk (POSTGRES_DATA_DIR=/tmp/ai-trader-pgdata or similar) and make it durable with logical backups to the network volume: pg_dump -Fc every 5 minutes and on SIGTERM to /workspace/backups (keep last 48, write to temp file then rename, verify with pg_restore --list), and automatic restore at startup when the data dir is empty and a valid dump exists. Redis may stay on /workspace (no mode-bit requirement; verify). Network volume stays the durable home for dumps, logs and data lake. Accepted loss window: up to 5 minutes of paper-trading rows after a crash. Before any live trading, move to managed PostgreSQL (D-005); this is not acceptable for live. Do NOT run postgres directly on the network volume. Implemented as T-018.
